data.cultural_impact: Andal's life and works continue to inspire and influence Tamil literature and culture. She is revered as an important figure in the Alvar tradition, a group of 12 poet-saints who have contributed significantly to the Bhakti movement in India. Andal's love poems have been set to music and sung as devotional songs called 'Tiruppavai' and 'Periya Tirumozhi'. Her legacy as a poet-saint continues to be celebrated in Tamil Nadu through various festivals and rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: Andal's life and works represent the spiritual journey of a soul in search of the divine. She embodies the idea of selfless love and devotion towards God, freely surrendering herself to his divine grace. Andal's poems express her longing and yearning for the ultimate truth, her search for spiritual understanding and enlightenment. Her life story is a reminder of the transformative power of love and devotion and the possibility of merging with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Andal is a divine female form in Hinduism, symbolizing pure devotion and passionate love for Lord Vishnu. Her name means 'one who is always immersed in Lord Vishnu's feet'. Andal's life and poetry exemplify the transformative power of deep devotion.

historical_references.reference: Andal was a Tamil poetess and saint, considered as one of the twelve Alvars, a group of poet-saints in Bhakti movement in medieval Tamil Nadu.
historical_references.context: Andal is revered as a goddess and a devotee of Lord Vishnu in the Hindu tradition.
